course_name_original: Fundamentos matemáticos de la ingeniería ii

learning_outcomes.text: Applies correctly the mathematical principles that may arise in engineering: linear algebra, geometry, differential geometry, differential and integral calculus, differential and partial differential equations, numerical methods, numerical algorithms, statistics and optimization.

Acquires the ability to use basic mathematical tools in modeling and solving situations related to engineering. The techniques studied are related to linear algebra and univariate and multivariate analysis. Understands the concept and acquires the most common analytical and numerical techniques related to solving differential equations and applies them to mathematical models related to engineering.

syllabus_topics: Multivariate analysis. Advanced concepts of differentiation. Solving optimization problems; Lagrange multipliers. Multiple integrals and applications.
Ordinary differential equations. Introduction to ordinary differential equations. Analytical solutions of first and second order linear equations.
Partial differential equations. Introduction to partial differential equations. Separable variables.
Complements. Laplace transforms and Fourier series.
assessment_rules: Students must obtain a minimum of 3.5 in each mixed test to be averaged. For the second attempt (resit), there are two options: Option A is to retake the entire syllabus, and Option B is to retake only one of the two parts if its score was below 3.5. By default, all students are registered for Option A; Option B must be requested via email before a specified date. During assessment tests, mobile phones, tablets, and other unauthorized electronic devices must be switched off and out of sight.
